title: Geometric regularity tested on finitely generated field extensions
statement: Let $k$ be a field and let $A$ be a Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] $k$-algebra which is geometrically regular over $k$ in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-g-ring] (that is, $k'\otimes_kA$ is a regular ring for every finite purely inseparable field extension $k'/k$). Then for every finitely generated field extension $K/k$ [def-pc-field-extension] (i.e. $K=k(a_1,\dots,a_n)$ for finitely many $a_1,\dots,a_n\in K$; for instance any finite extension) the ring $K\otimes_kA$ is Noetherian and regular, i.e. every localization of $K\otimes_kA$ at a prime ideal is a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme].

source.place: Lemma Tag 0381 (lemma-geometrically-regular, line 47104), implication (2) => (1), and its proof (Lemmas 030R make-separable, 037X localization-smooth-separable, 00T4 base-change-smooth, 07NF regular-goes-up, 07NG descent-regular); Noetherianity of $K\otimes_kA$: Lemma Tag 045I (lemma-Noetherian-field-extension, line 6166)

proof.text: (Setup: making $K$ separable.) Let $K/k$ be a finitely generated field extension, $K=k(a_1,\dots,a_n)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-make-separable] there are a field $K'$ with a field homomorphism $\iota:K\to K'$ and a subfield $k'\subseteq K'$ containing the image of $k$, with $k'/k$ and $K'/K$ finite purely inseparable [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension] and $K'/k'$ separable [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension]; the two $k$-algebra structures on $K'$ (through $k\to K\xrightarrow{\iota}K'$ and through $k\subseteq k'\subseteq K'$) agree, and we regard $K'$ as a $k$-algebra in this way. The extension $K'/k'$ is finitely generated [def-pc-field-extension]: if $e_1,\dots,e_m$ is a $K$-basis of $K'$ (finite since $K'/K$ is finite), every element of $K'$ is a $K$-linear combination of the $e_j$ and $K=k(a_1,\dots,a_n)$, so $K'=k(\iota(a_1),\dots,\iota(a_n),e_1,\dots,e_m)$, and a fortiori $K'=k'(\iota(a_1),\dots,\iota(a_n),e_1,\dots,e_m)$ since $k\subseteq k'\subseteq K'$.

proof.text: (A smooth model of $K'$.) $K'/k'$ is a finitely generated separable field extension (Step 1), so by [lem-weil-pbc-separable-extension-fraction-field-of-smooth-algebra] there is a $k'$-subalgebra $B\subseteq K'$ such that $k'\to B$ is smooth [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map] and $K'$ is the fraction field of $B$. Thus $B$ is a domain, $M=B\setminus\{0\}$ is a multiplicative subset of $B$, and the inclusion $B\to K'$ is a localization of $B$ at $M$: elements of $M$ are invertible in the field $K'$, every element of $K'$ is $b/b'$ with $b'\in M$, and $b\mapsto0$ in $K'$ means $b=0$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 0381 (lemma-geometrically-regular, line 47104), (2) => (1): 'By Lemma 037X (lemma-localization-smooth-separable) there exists a smooth k'-algebra B such that K' is the fraction field of B'

proof.text: (Stacks Step 1: $C=k'\otimes_kA$ is regular.) $A$ is Noetherian and geometrically regular over $k$, and $k'/k$ is a finite purely inseparable extension (Step 1); by the definition of geometric regularity in [def-weil-pbc-g-ring] the ring $C:=k'\otimes_kA$ is regular [def-weil-regular-scheme]. We regard $C$ as a $k'$-algebra through $c\mapsto c\otimes1$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 0381 (lemma-geometrically-regular, line 47104), (2) => (1), Step 1

proof.text: (Stacks Step 2: $D=C\otimes_{k'}B$ is regular.) Since $k'\to B$ is smooth (Step 2), its base change along $k'\to C$, the ring map $C\to D:=C\otimes_{k'}B$, $c\mapsto c\otimes1$, is smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-base-change-composition] (1). As $C$ is a regular ring (Step 3), ascent of regularity along smooth ring maps [lem-weil-pbc-regular-ring-smooth-ascent] shows that $D$ is a regular ring [def-weil-regular-scheme].

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 0381 (lemma-geometrically-regular, line 47104), (2) => (1), Step 2 (Lemma 00T4 lemma-base-change-smooth and Lemma 07NF lemma-regular-goes-up)

proof.text: (Stacks Step 3: $K'\otimes_kA$ is regular.) Regard $D=C\otimes_{k'}B$ as a $B$-algebra through $\psi:B\to D$, $b\mapsto1\otimes b$. By Step 2, $B\to K'$ is a localization of $B$ at $M=B\setminus\{0\}$, so by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-base-change] the ring map $D\to D\otimes_BK'$, $x\mapsto x\otimes1$, is a localization of $D$ at $\psi(M)$. Next, $D\otimes_BK'=(C\otimes_{k'}B)\otimes_BK'\cong K'\otimes_B(B\otimes_{k'}C)$ by the symmetry of the tensor product, and $K'\otimes_B(B\otimes_{k'}C)\cong K'\otimes_{k'}C$, $y\otimes(b\otimes c)\mapsto by\otimes c$, by [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-cancel-base-change] (with $R=k'$, $S=B$, the $R$-algebra $C$ and the $S$-algebra $K'$); and $K'\otimes_{k'}C=K'\otimes_{k'}(k'\otimes_kA)\cong K'\otimes_kA$, $y\otimes(c\otimes a)\mapsto cy\otimes a$, again by [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-cancel-base-change] (with $R=k$, $S=k'$, the $k$-algebra $A$ and the $k'$-algebra $K'$). Composing a localization with a ring isomorphism gives a localization (conditions (a)-(c) are transported by the isomorphism), so $K'\otimes_kA$ is isomorphic to a localization of the regular ring $D$ (Step 4) at a multiplicative subset, hence is a regular ring by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-of-regular-ring]; a ring isomorphic to a regular ring is regular (Noetherianity and the localizations at corresponding primes are transported) [def-weil-regular-scheme].

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 0381 (lemma-geometrically-regular, line 47104), (2) => (1), Step 3 ('K' otimes_{k'} k' otimes_k A = K' otimes_k A is a regular ring as it is a localization of a regular ring (immediate from the definition)')

proof.text: (Stacks Step 4: descent to $K\otimes_kA$.) Put $E:=K\otimes_kA$, a $K$-algebra through $x\mapsto x\otimes1$. By [lem-weil-pbc-field-extension-base-change-faithfully-flat], applied to the field extension $\iota:K\to K'$ and the $K$-algebra $E$, the ring map $E\to E\otimes_KK'$, $e\mapsto e\otimes1$, is faithfully flat [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map]. By the symmetry of the tensor product and [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-cancel-base-change] (with $R=k$, $S=K$, the $k$-algebra $A$ and the $K$-algebra $K'$; its $k$-algebra structure is the one fixed in Step 1), $E\otimes_KK'\cong K'\otimes_K(K\otimes_kA)\cong K'\otimes_kA$, and the composite $E\to K'\otimes_kA$ sends $x\otimes a\mapsto(x\otimes a)\otimes1\mapsto1\otimes(x\otimes a)\mapsto\iota(x)\otimes a$. A faithfully flat ring map followed by a ring isomorphism is faithfully flat (the module structures correspond), so $E\to K'\otimes_kA$, $x\otimes a\mapsto\iota(x)\otimes a$, is faithfully flat, and its target is a regular ring by Step 5. By descent of regularity along faithfully flat ring maps [lem-weil-pbc-regular-ring-faithfully-flat-descent], $E=K\otimes_kA$ is a regular ring [def-weil-regular-scheme]: it is Noetherian and every localization at a prime ideal is a regular local ring. This is the claim. (The Noetherianity of $K\otimes_kA$, which Stacks gets beforehand from Lemma 045I lemma-Noetherian-field-extension only to make the statement meaningful, is part of the conclusion of [lem-weil-pbc-regular-ring-faithfully-flat-descent], so 045I is not needed.)
